title: Propagate the merit-over-cost recommendation rule to implementer/reviewer/auditor and make it user-visible for cam-runtime adopters
description:
Operator directive 2026-07-20 (Eduardo), to be canonical for cam-cli AND for everyone who downloads and runs cam-runtime: no LLM recommendation may be the one of lowest operational cost. Recommendations rank by robustness, launch-readiness and industry standard. Human implementation time is NOT a valid tiebreaker -- the entire point of using an LLM is to buy that time back, so implementation effort, token spend and operational cost must not downgrade what is recommended.

MEASURED GAP (2026-07-20, grep over .claude/agents/, templates/, scripts/cam/CLAUDE.md):
- CARRIES the rule: subagent-orchestrator.md, subagent-planner.md (both in .claude/ and templates/), plus templates/skills/spec-with-docs/SKILL.md.
- MISSING the rule: subagent-implementer.md, subagent-reviewer.md, subagent-auditor.md -- in BOTH .claude/ and templates/.

The rule currently lives in the two agents that THINK and is absent from the three that BUILD, APPROVE and GATE. That is backwards: it binds where it matters least. The reviewer gap is the most severe, since the reviewer is the last gate -- if it does not hold the bar, a cheap-but-weak implementation passes and nothing downstream catches it. The auditor gap lets a cost-optimized PRD get approved before any code is written. The implementer gap is the one already corrected by hand before (see memory/feedback-recommend-on-merits-not-effort.md: the rule extends to EXECUTION -- no gambiarras or shortcuts, always the robust root-cause fix; a shortcut is legitimate only to unblock something extremely necessary).

SCOPE:
- Add the rule to subagent-implementer.md, subagent-reviewer.md, subagent-auditor.md, phrased per role (implementer: execution, root-cause over shortcut; reviewer: flag cost-motivated weakness as a finding, do not accept 'good enough for v1' as a rationale; auditor: do not approve a PRD whose scope was trimmed for effort reasons).
- Apply to BOTH .claude/agents/ and templates/agents/. templates/ is what ships to adopters, so a fix that lands only in .claude/ leaves every downstream user with the same hole. CHECK THE DUAL-COPY FIRST: .claude/ and templates/ are NOT uniformly byte-identical; diff before assuming, and run `bun run embed-vendor:check` (regenerate via `bun run embed-vendor`) since templates/ is touched.
- Make it user-visible to adopters in prose, not only in LLM-consumed agent files. A human evaluating cam-runtime should be able to read this stance without opening .claude/agents/*.md. README or docs/ is the right surface; pick one and state it once.

TWO CLAUSES THAT MUST SURVIVE THE REDACTION -- omitting either turns the rule into a defect:
(1) THE RULE LIMITS QUALITY, NOT SCOPE. Reuse the existing orchestrator/planner phrasing: Simplicity remains the SCOPE limiter; this rule limits the QUALITY of the recommendation within that scope. Without this clause, 'always the most robust' licenses speculative abstraction in the implementer and oversized PRDs in the planner. Not hypothetical: PRDs of 8-9+ stories historically blow through the 3-round review budget (CAM-53, CAM-101, CAM-109).
(2) OPERATIONAL COST IS NEVER A CRITERION, BUT CONTEXT EXHAUSTION IS A QUALITY CRITERION. Token spend and compute cost must not decide anything. Context-window exhaustion is different in kind: it DEGRADES output quality and is a physical limit, not an economy. The one-PR-per-session invariant in subagent-orchestrator.md exists precisely for this reason. If the rule ships as 'always the most expensive path, no exceptions' it contradicts a shipped invariant. Phrase it as: cost is never a criterion; quality degradation from context exhaustion is a quality criterion, not a cost one.

PRIOR ART to stay consistent with: the existing block in .claude/agents/subagent-orchestrator.md ('rank by engineering merit (quality, launch-readiness), never by execution cost... This is quality-within-scope, not gold-plating'), the global user CLAUDE.md section 1, and memory/feedback-recommend-on-merits-not-effort.md.

NEEDS REBUILD: templates/ is embedded at build time via embed-vendor, so the binary must be rebuilt for adopters to receive the change.

spec.scope: Propagate the operator's merit-over-cost recommendation rule (recommendations rank by robustness / launch-readiness / industry standard, never by operational cost, implementation effort, or token spend) to the three cam agents that BUILD, GATE, and APPROVE: subagent-implementer, subagent-reviewer, subagent-auditor. Apply it in BOTH .claude/agents/ and templates/agents/ (templates/ ships to cam-runtime adopters). Add per-role framing plus one shared verbatim two-clause sentence, then make the stance user-visible to adopters as human prose in docs/agent-readiness.md. Regenerate the embedded vendor blob after touching templates/. OUT OF SCOPE: subagent-planner (this issue scopes only the three build/gate/approve agents) and any code/runtime change.
acceptanceCriteria: subagent-implementer carries the rule, framed for EXECUTION (always the robust root-cause fix over a shortcut; a shortcut is legitimate only to unblock something extremely necessary), and includes the verbatim shared sentence. [oracle: grep -q "context-window exhaustion is a quality criterion" .claude/agents/subagent-implementer.md]

subagent-reviewer carries the rule, framed for REVIEW (flag a cost-motivated or effort-motivated weakness as a finding; do not accept 'good enough for v1' as a rationale for a weaker implementation), including the verbatim shared sentence. [oracle: grep -q "context-window exhaustion is a quality criterion" .claude/agents/subagent-reviewer.md]

subagent-auditor carries the rule, framed for AUDIT (do not APPROVE a PRD whose scope or quality was trimmed for effort/cost reasons), including the verbatim shared sentence. [oracle: grep -q "context-window exhaustion is a quality criterion" .claude/agents/subagent-auditor.md]

The templates/ copy of subagent-implementer carries the identical shared sentence (adopters get the same rule). [oracle: grep -q "context-window exhaustion is a quality criterion" templates/agents/subagent-implementer.md]
The templates/ copy of subagent-reviewer carries the identical shared sentence. [oracle: grep -q "context-window exhaustion is a quality criterion" templates/agents/subagent-reviewer.md]
The templates/ copy of subagent-auditor carries the identical shared sentence. [oracle: grep -q "context-window exhaustion is a quality criterion" templates/agents/subagent-auditor.md]
The embedded vendor blob is regenerated from the edited templates/ and the repo stays self-consistent. [oracle: bun run embed-vendor:check && bun test test/embedded.test.ts]

docs/agent-readiness.md states the stance as human-readable prose (no em-dash, no decorative emoji per repo human-doc convention) under the existing 'Where cam is already ahead of the rubric' section, so a human evaluating cam-runtime reads it without opening any agent file. [oracle: grep -q "never by operational cost" docs/agent-readiness.md]

Every redaction preserves BOTH must-survive clauses (clause 1: the rule limits QUALITY not SCOPE, Simplicity remains the scope limiter; clause 2: operational cost is never a criterion but quality degradation from context-window exhaustion is a quality criterion, not a cost one), uses correct per-role framing, and is consistent with the prior-art block in subagent-orchestrator.md and memory/feedback-recommend-on-merits-not-effort.md. [oracle: reviewer-judgment]
gotchas: DICTATED VERBATIM shared sentence that MUST appear identically in all six agent .md copies (it carries both must-survive clauses and is what the grep oracles key on): 'This rule limits the quality of the recommendation, not its scope: Simplicity remains the scope limiter. Operational cost is never a criterion, but quality degradation from context-window exhaustion is a quality criterion, not a cost one.' Add per-role lead-in prose around it; do not alter this sentence.

DUAL-COPY IS NOT BYTE-IDENTICAL. .claude/agents/*.md are cam-cli-specialized; templates/agents/*.md are the generic portable version. The added rule is project-agnostic prose so its text is identical in both copies, but insertion points differ per file. Do NOT anchor the insertion to a cam-cli-only heading (e.g. the auditor's '### F. Project-specific sanity (cam-cli)'); place it in a section that exists in each variant. This is an ADDITIVE edit, never a reconcile of the two copies.

templates/ is embedded into src/vendor/_generated.ts at build time. After editing templates/agents/*.md you MUST run `bun run embed-vendor` to regenerate src/vendor/_generated.ts, or `bun run embed-vendor:check` (wired into check:all/CI and test/embedded.test.ts) fails.

EM-DASH RULE SPLITS BY AUDIENCE: .claude/agents/*.md and templates/agents/*.md are LLM-consumed, so em-dash and emoji are fine there. docs/agent-readiness.md is human-readable persisted markdown, so its paragraph must use no em-dash (use colon/comma/parentheses/period) and no decorative emoji.

This is docs/governance only: no src/ runtime code changes. The .claude/agents/ edits take effect for the running sidecar's next agent spawn without a rebuild (agent docs are read from disk); the templates/ + _generated.ts change matters only for `cam init` in fresh adopter projects, but still regenerate the blob so CI passes.

PRIOR ART to reuse for phrasing consistency: the merit block in .claude/agents/subagent-orchestrator.md ('rank by engineering merit (quality, launch-readiness), never by execution cost ... This is quality-within-scope, not gold-plating'), and memory/feedback-recommend-on-merits-not-effort.md.
domainTerms: merit-over-cost rule: recommendations rank by robustness/launch-readiness/industry-standard, never by operational cost, implementation effort, or token spend
must-survive clause 1: the rule limits QUALITY not SCOPE (Simplicity stays the scope limiter)
must-survive clause 2: operational cost is never a criterion, but context-window exhaustion IS a quality criterion
embed-vendor: bun script that embeds vendor/ and templates/ into src/vendor/_generated.ts
